paper_title: Particle Physics Implications of a Recent Test of the Gravitational Inverse Square Law
suggested_experiment_name: Torsion-balance test of gravitational inverse-square law (Ref. [1])
coupling_convention: g_b (dimensionless scalar baryon coupling), as plotted on y-axis labeled 'g_b^S λ / (4πrc)'
notes: Paper presents constraints on multiple exotic interactions from a torsion-balance test of the gravitational inverse-square law. Primary results are presented as constraints on Yukawa-type interactions (scalar/vector boson exchange), radion/dilaton exchange, chameleon fields, and power-law potentials. While the pre-analysis hint suggests ScalarBaryon, the paper does NOT present data in a standard (mass, coupling) format suitable for extraction. Instead: (1) Scalar/vector Yukawa constraints are shown in Figures 1-2 as functions of mass and charge parameter ψ̃, but no explicit numerical (m, g) pairs are tabulated. (2) Radion/dilaton bounds are given as lower limits on unification mass M* (Eqs. 9-10), not as coupling vs. mass exclusion curves. (3) Chameleon constraints (Fig. 4) are in the (β, γ) parameter space, not standard coupling-mass format. (4) Power-law constraints (Table I) give dimensionless coefficients β_k for k=2,3,4,5 but these are not mass-dependent couplings. (5) γ5-pseudoscalar constraints (Fig. 5) show bounds on g_P^n vs. mass, but the figure is not sufficiently resolved to extract precise numerical points. The paper's primary contribution is methodological (applying ISL data to constrain exotic forces) rather than providing a clean exclusion curve in standard (m_eV, coupling) format. Extraction confidence is low because: (a) coupling type is ambiguous (could be ScalarBaryon, ScalarNucleon, or AxionCPV depending on interpretation), (b) data are presented in non-standard parameter spaces (ψ̃, β, γ, β_k) rather than direct coupling-mass pairs, and (c) figures lack sufficient resolution for reliable point extraction. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 1 shows 95% confidence constraints on scalar or vector Yukawa interactions from a torsion-balance test of the gravitational inverse-square law. The x-axis is labeled 'mc² [meV]' and ranges from 0.1 to 10 meV (converted to eV: 1e5 to 1e7 eV). The y-axis is labeled 'g_b^S λ / (4πrc)' on the left and 'g_b^S / (4πrc) [GeV^-2]' on the right, with range 10^-5 to 10^3. The yellow shaded region above the boundary is EXCLUDED. The boundary shows a characteristic shape: nearly flat at low mass (~1e-4 coupling), then rising steeply at higher masses. The plot constrains scalar baryon couplings from dilaton/radion/chameleon exchange forces. Confidence level is 95% as stated in figure caption.
